question: Should OpenClaw permit gateway.auth.mode none on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement is required if it does?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally blocks reachable unauthenticated Gateway startup, while the requested behavior would move operator-surface protection from OpenClaw auth to external network controls.

options.title: Keep Fail-Closed Boundary
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and point private deployments at the supported delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor Private-Ingress Opt-In
options.body: Allow reachable no-auth only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, documentation, and focused tests.

options.title: Reject Reachable No-Auth Core Mode
options.body: Close the direction as not planned after documenting why OpenClaw core will not support unauthenticated reachable Gateway binds.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Closed Boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and point private deployments at the supported delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway auth hardening and trusted-proxy review history make this the strongest available owner for the security-boundary decision.
